## PowerPoint and Word Examples {#sec-office-examples}

**maidr** reads the charts of a PowerPoint presentation and of a Word document.
Pass a `.pptx` file to `maidr.read_powerpoint_charts()`, or a `.docx` file to
`maidr.read_word_charts()`, and hand any chart either returns to
`maidr.show()`, `maidr.render()` or `maidr.save_html()`: the chart can then be
read from the keyboard, as sound, as text and in braille. None of PowerPoint,
Word or Excel needs to be installed. For the charts of a workbook, see the
[Excel](examples-excel.qmd) page.

::: {.callout-warning title="Experimental"}
PowerPoint and Word support is **experimental**. What it reads, and how, may
change without a deprecation period, whichever chart type is read: see
[Plot Type Stability](stability.qmd#powerpoint-and-word-support).
:::

A chart on a slide or in a document is the chart Excel draws: the same chart
part, with the same copy of the values it shows, and its data in a workbook
embedded in the file beside it. So it is read just as the
[Excel page](examples-excel.qmd) describes, every chart type Excel draws
included, from column charts to waterfalls and treemaps. The embedded workbook
is read only for what the copy leaves out: an axis with no title is named after
the header cell above its categories in the chart's data sheet. Each chart is
drawn again with matplotlib, in the colors of its slide's or its document's
theme.

The examples read [slides.pptx](slides.pptx), a presentation of quarterly
sales with a chart on each of three slides, the last of them hidden, and
[report.docx](report.docx), a short report with two charts.

### Reading a Presentation

`maidr.read_powerpoint_charts()` returns the charts slide by slide, in slide
show order, each with the number of its slide, whether that slide is hidden,
its name and its title. The charts of hidden slides are read too.

```{python}
#| warning: false
import maidr

slides = maidr.read_powerpoint_charts("slides.pptx")
for chart in slides:
    print(chart.slide, chart.hidden, chart.name, chart.title, sep=" | ")
```

Save every chart of a presentation as its own page with a loop:

```python
for chart in maidr.read_powerpoint_charts("slides.pptx"):
    maidr.save_html(chart, f"slide-{chart.slide}-{chart.name}.html")
```

Both functions also take an open binary file, such as the one a Streamlit or
Shiny upload control hands you.

### Column Chart on a Slide

Each region is a series and each quarter a category: the left and right arrow
keys move between quarters, and up and down between the regions. The category
axis has no title on the slide, so it is named after the header above the
quarters in the chart's data sheet, *Quarter*.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Clustered column chart of revenue by quarter for the North and South regions
maidr.show(slides[0])
```

### Line Chart on a Slide

The margin is read as a percentage, because its data sheet formats it as one.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Line chart of the margin by quarter
maidr.show(slides[1])
```

### Pie Chart on a Hidden Slide

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Pie chart of the share of revenue by region
maidr.show(slides[2])
```

### Reading a Document

`maidr.read_word_charts()` returns the charts of the document's body in
reading order, inline and floating ones and those in tables and text boxes,
each with its place among the document's charts, its name and its title.

```{python}
#| warning: false
report = maidr.read_word_charts("report.docx")
for chart in report:
    print(chart.number, chart.name, chart.title, sep=" | ")
```

### Line Chart in a Document

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Line chart of visitors by month, January to June
maidr.show(report[0])
```

### Bar Chart in a Document

The teams are named after the header above them in the chart's data sheet,
*Team*.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Horizontal bar chart of tickets closed by team
maidr.show(report[1])
```
